newsitem.title: ROMANIA: BUCHAREST BOURSE TO HOLD THREE WEEKLY SESSIONS.
newsitem.headline: BUCHAREST BOURSE TO HOLD THREE WEEKLY SESSIONS.

text.p: The Bucharest stock exchange said on Thursday it would hold three trading sessions per week from next week instead of the present two.
Exchange spokesman George Chrita said trading would now take place on Wednesday in addition to Tuesday and Thursday.
He said each trading day would open at 9.15 a.m. (0715 GMT) with a 15-minute pre-opening session, followed by four hours of continuous trading.
From 1.30 p.m. (1130 GMT) traders will have an hour to work out their reports and introduce orders for the next session, Chirita said.
Brokers welcomed the decision. "This is a well-considered move now, when volumes are a lot higher and when you have more stocks to trade in," said one.

The Bucharest bourse, which saw sluggish activity for most of 1996, has put on a fine show since the start of the year, with volumes and most prices on the rise. Turnver hit an all-time peak of 6.3 billion lei in mid-February. The previous record was 1.7 billion last March.
It now trades 22 stocks, of which two are listed on the first tier, where qualification criteria are tougher.
